Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Latin word

negō

negō, negāre, negāvī, negātum

verb, first conjugation; with an accusative, or an accusative and infinitive

deny, say that … not; refuse, say no to; say no; say that … not

In this lexicon

  • deny

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Ad. 799: Factum est; nōn negō.; Cic. Fin. 2.68 (Lewis & Short): Stōicī negant quidquam esse bonum, nisi quod honestum sit

  • deny

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 8.4.2: numquam reō cuiquam … tam praecīsē negāvī quam hic mihi; Caes. B.G. 5.6 (Lewis & Short): postquam id obstinātē sibi negārī videt

  • say

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 2.8.1: quaerō ecquid litterārum. negant.

Examples

  • Negat quis? negō: ait? ajō.

    Someone says no? I say no. He says yes? I say yes.Ter. Eun. 252

    In the entry for deny

  • Factum est; nōn negō.

    It’s done; I don’t deny it.Ter. Ad. 799

    In the entry for deny

  • Nēmō it īnfitiās.

    No one denies it.Plaut. Curc. 489

    In the entry for deny

  • metuō, sī tibi dēnegem quod mē ōrās, nē tē leviōrem ergā mē putēs

    I’m afraid that if I refuse what you ask me, you’ll think I value you lessPlaut. Trin. 1170–1171

    In the entry for deny

  • numquam reō cuiquam tam humilī, tam sordidō, tam nocentī, tam aliēnō tam praecīsē negāvī quam hic mihi

    I never refused any defendant, however low, mean, guilty or remote from me, as flatly as he refused meCic. Att. 8.4.2
